# Owned Unix compress inputs

Payloads and generator code are project-owned and redistributable under the repository license. The phrase is `abracadabra abracadabra\n` repeated six times. `pattern(n)` uses xorshift32 seed `0x6d2b79f5`, shifts 13/17/5 and each resulting high byte. `random.Z` contains 90,000 pattern bytes; `natural-clear.Z` contains the phrase repeated 4000 times followed by 250,000 pattern bytes. Empty and zero inputs are explicit. `files.taz` wraps the existing owned `streams/files.txz` TAR bytes. `empty.taz` is the same 1024 zero bytes through a TAR candidate; `bad-header.Z` wraps the existing owned bad-header.txz TAR bytes and must fail TAR admission. These nine inputs are generated by the public ncompress compressor.

The remaining inputs are generated by owned textbook LZW and explicit code packing: every maximum width 9–16 with `2 * 2^bits + 2048` pattern bytes, `nonblock-width.Z` with 5000 pattern bytes and maximum 12, `nonblock.Z` with codes 65/66/256/258 producing `ABABABA`, and `clear.Z` with codes 65/66/257/CLEAR then 67/68/257 producing `ABABCDCD`. The last two exercise actual dictionary references and the undefined-next-code case; they are not stored-only substitutes for LZW coverage.

The independent reference [ncompress 1.0.2](https://github.com/valgur/ncompress) wheel is `ncompress-1.0.2-cp312-abi3-win_amd64.whl`, SHA-256 `672f7166abf634df43a592ec2d1053c991057a1f7020d55288fa03ab60ebae98`. Its public compressor and decompressor are local references only; all installed runtime files are compared with the pinned wheel, excluding the installer's rewritten RECORD. It is distributed under the author's Unlicense/public-domain terms. No reference implementation source or binary is included in product or fixture files.

The second reader is [7-Zip 26.06](https://github.com/ip7z/7zip/releases/tag/26.06), extracted without running its installer. The author installer SHA-256 is `9b697f65ecc2d9b0152f5ee96d72dde522a7827690349d9307935dacf40f42ec`; `7z.exe` is `dc0493429fe28136fcb177a0e77c9875cbb3b0bff5f2f8eeba4df302e98cef76`, and `7z.dll` is `500db9eb17f3c21b729ba41dd02ecfe1823da05028c7e4ba129084cc74cc364e`. All 20 inputs decode correctly in fixed ncompress. Nineteen also decode correctly in pinned 7-Zip; saturated `width-9.Z` produces only 256 bytes and a data error in that reference. This is an explicit reference limitation, associated with the historical [9-bit discussion](https://github.com/vapier/ncompress/issues/5), and is not recorded as a second-reader pass.

Keep references under `build/toolchain/references/`. Using a compatible Python, run `scripts/generate-compress-fixtures.py --reference build/toolchain/references/ncompress-1.0.2 --sevenzip build/toolchain/references/7zip-26.06-full`; add `--check` to compare without rewriting inputs. The generator verifies reference identities, complete decoded bytes and the exact saturated-9-bit limitation. Its result manifest remains under `build/review/format-expansion/`. Native macOS/Linux reference tools require their own verified identities; this Windows reference setup is not evidence for those platforms.

Canonical input identities for **FORMAT-COMPRESS** follow. Decoded sizes describe the raw Z output; `bad-header.Z` has intentionally invalid TAR metadata.
